abstract: Landau's theorem turns a growth bound $F\ll e^{\varphi}$ on $\sigma\ge1-1/\psi(t)$, for $F=\exp\int x^{-s}dm$ with $dm\ge0$ and a simple pole at $1$, into a zero-free region $\sigma\ge1-c/(\psi\varphi)$. The best constant is a property of Beurling zeta functions. Broucke showed that it is at most $2$ when the zeros lie on a contour $1-\beta=f(\log\gamma)$ with $f$ convex, regularly varying and $uf(u)\to\infty$, and an earlier paper lowered this to $0.4124$ on the same class. We extend the upper bound in four directions. First, the harmonic factors of that construction need only an integrable resolvent instead of $L^1$ norm below $1$; certified data then give $c^*<0.4086$. Second, smoothing the data with a Gevrey kernel removes the condition $uf(u)\to\infty$: the bound $0.4086$ holds for every continuous decreasing $f$ with $f(u+h)/f(u)\to1$, including regions narrower than the classical one. Third, a single example gives $0.4086$ for every pair $(2\lambda,\log t/\lambda)$ of Diamond, Montgomery and Vorhauer's class with $\log t/\lambda\ll e^{2\lambda}$ (the range of Landau's theorem) and $\lambda$ mildly regular, where only $2$ was known. Fourth, the bound holds for discrete systems of generalized primes, for contours with two mild extra conditions (for example $f(u)=u^{-\alpha}$, $\alpha>0$): the Broucke-Vindas random approximation, with a trivial bound for the small primes, loses only $O(\log\log\log t)$ in the growth. As a consequence, the constants $1$ and $1/(1+\alpha)$ proposed by Broucke and Révész fail for every such $f$ and every $\alpha\in[0,1)$. The results concern the Beurling class, not the zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Resubmission after the review of submission xXe7D0h64_jkgVr-. The certificate is rebuilt on the Paper 93 certificate with all its rounding controls: the gamma_K a posteriori residual allowance, rounding of Phi, of the trigonometric sums and of the angle grid, the inflated nu-hat bound, and the exact cell maximum of v nu(v) with interior vertices (fixing the n=4 underestimate). The exact data are defined (nu normalised by its exact integral), the 1+1e-13 inflation is removed, and computed-versus-exact data differences are bounded and propagated. Each remaining inflation factor is justified in a code comment. The supplement includes the line-by-line diff against the Paper 93 certificate. Results: 1.3705e-4 (n=6, 0.4086) and 2.2394e-4 (n=4, 0.4154); both controls fail. Text: Corollary 3.3 describes the data and the certificate; Lemma 4.3(i) uses the window [0,1+eps]; Corollary 7.1 states its assumptions; references are numbered.
title: The constant in Landau's zero-free region theorem is below 0.41 for narrow contours, classical width and discrete systems
